question: Why does the 132831 panorama match only 9.1 GSR players per frame (132877: 15.2)? detection or geometry?

gsr_foot_points_through_our_landmark_cal.note: GSR image foot (u,v) projected with our 65-landmark TPS calibration vs the GSR pitch coordinate: a systematic +2..3 m shift along pitch y, independent of our detector
gsr_foot_points_through_our_landmark_cal.retraction: WITHDRAWN on 2026-11-02: GSR pixels are panorama pixels (visual overlay); see gsr-reference-geometry.json — the 4.5/3.5 m figure stands as a measurement of the GSR geometry bias

organisers_homography_npy: units/convention unknown (errors ~10^3), not usable for arbitration
reading: detection is not the limit at 132831 (v2 recall 96.1%, precision 91.6% on the MOT clip; 22.4 tracked players per frame vs 22 in GSR). The low GSR match rate comes from a systematic 2-3 m offset along pitch width between the landmark-based calibration and the GSR pitch coordinates, largest in the far half; with a 6 m radius 82-96% of GSR players have a tracked counterpart (so the players are detected; the disagreement is positional). Which side is right cannot be settled from these files; our calibration is validated on official pitch markings (LOO 1.57 m). GSR-based matched counts and defensive-line errors therefore carry a reference bias; label-level agreement (team, block label) is affected less because the bias is along y while block depth is along x.

independent_ruler_attempts.gsr_table_homography: image->pitch fitted from the GSR table itself is not a planar homography of the panorama (inliers 36%/47%, landmarks off by 12-18 m): GSR pixel coordinates are in another image space, so they cannot arbitrate

throw_in_touchline.idea: the thrower stands on the touchline (y=0/68); compare tracked vs GSR y of the nearest player to the event position
throw_in_touchline.result: inconclusive: tracked positions are clamped to the pitch (0..100) so touchline distances read 0.0, GSR shows the same clamping; in the two unclamped cases tracked was 1.0-1.5 m further inside than GSR, consistent with the far-half +y offset but too few to decide who is right

independent_ruler_attempts.status: RESOLVED in gsr-reference-geometry.json: the bias is on the GSR side relative to official markings
